# Acts of Thomas — Chapter 10
**Agent:** SOPHIA (Consensus)
**Source:** Syriac MS / Greek recension, Acts of Thomas 10

---

## Consensus Translation

*[After the Hymn. Mygdonia and Charisius. Thomas imprisoned.]*

1. When Thomas had finished the hymn, he returned to the city and found Mygdonia on the road.

2. She said: "Where have you been, man of God? I have been searching for you."

3. Thomas said: "I was singing praise to my Lord. Now tell me what you need."

4. Mygdonia said: "My husband Charisius is greatly troubled on account of you, for he has heard that I have forsaken him and received instruction from you. I beg you — leave this city, lest harm come to you."

5. Thomas said: "Have no fear. My Lord Jesus Christ, who has sent me, will protect me. But go to your husband and treat him gently."

6. Mygdonia said: "I cannot return to him as before, for I have received the seal of the Lord."

7. Thomas said: "The seal of the Lord is holy and pure; all who receive and keep it are made holy with him."

8. She returned to her house.

9. Her husband Charisius was waiting and was furious. He said: "Where have you been, and who has stolen you away from me?"

10. Mygdonia said: "I have not been stolen. I have heard words of eternal life and I have believed."

11. Charisius said: "What is this eternal life and what teaching have you received?"

12. Mygdonia said: "It cannot be described in words. If you wish to hear it, come with me and listen for yourself."

13. But Charisius was angry and would not listen, and he sent for Thomas.

14. Thomas came, and Charisius said: "Why have you led my wife astray? Why has she forsaken the marriage bed?"

15. Thomas said: "I have not led her astray. She has received the gift of God."

16. "What gift?" said Charisius.

17. Thomas said: "She has received the Holy Spirit, who is not subject to the things of this world."

18. Charisius was furious and went to the king, saying: "This stranger has bewitched my wife."

19. The king said: "Take this man and cast him into prison, and we shall see what will come of it."

20. Thomas was led to prison and gave thanks to God.

---

## Textual Notes

- **"Received the seal of the Lord" (v.6):** Baptism, here understood as creating a new identity that supersedes prior social obligations in Mygdonia's own estimation. Thomas does not instruct this; he responds to it.
- **"As before" (v.6):** Added by LOGOS — not in all witnesses, but contextually necessary. Mygdonia does not say she will never see her husband; she says she cannot return to the previous relationship.
- **"It cannot be described in words" (v.12):** Mygdonia's mystical claim. The gospel/eternal life she has received is ineffable — it must be directly heard.
- **"Bewitched my wife" (v.18):** Charisius's charge against Thomas is the standard accusation against itinerant apostles in the apocryphal acts — magic, seduction, sorcery. Thomas has done none of these; the charge reflects Charisius's inability to comprehend Mygdonia's autonomous decision.
- **"Gave thanks to God" (v.20):** A Pauline pattern (Acts 16:25, Phil 4:11) — imprisonment is met with thanksgiving.

---
*SOPHIA synthesis: Chapter 10 establishes the conflict that will drive the narrative to Thomas's death. Mygdonia's theological position is preserved with full integrity, Thomas's counsel of gentleness is not contradicted, and the social consequences are plainly stated.*
